props.title: Synthetic methanol process

props.name: any catalyst suitable for synthetic methanol production

evidence.quote: My process is in no way dependent on the use of a specific catalyst.
In general, any catalyst suitable for synthetic methanol pro-- go duction may be employed in the process, these . catalysts ordinarily consisting of mixtures of _ metallic oxides

props.note: the patent refers to catalysts described in U.S. Patents 1,558,559, 1,608,648(?), 1,609,593 and English Patents 229,714(?) and 229,715; the numbers are OCR readings

evidence.quote: circulated over a methanol catalyst contain-— Ing a mixture of zinc and chromium oxides for a period of 12 hours.

when the gas mixture passing over the catalyst comprises 1-5% carbon di- oxide and 99-95% hydrogen, the most favor- IS able results are obtained.

props.scope: gas mixture passing over the catalyst
props.statement: When the proportion of carbon dioxide to hydrogen is greatly decreased the methanol in the condensate approaches the theoretical figure (approximately 70%), undesirable side reactions being partially or wholly inhibited; the most favorable results are obtained with 1-5% carbon dioxide and 99-95% hydrogen in the gas passing over the catalyst.

props.name: 390 °C more favorable than 420 °C for purity

evidence.quote: Since the temperature — employed (390° C.) is a more favorable one, © the purity of the methanol thus produced — is greater;
is greater; for example, Experiment 7 pro- | duced a condensate containing practically the yg theoretical proportions of methanol and.

props.statement: The temperature of 390° C. (Table II) is a more favorable one than that of Table I; the purity of the methanol produced is greater, Experiment 7 giving practically the theoretical proportions of methanol and water.

props.name: above 5% CO2 in circulating gas, loss of gases

evidence.quote: However if this adjustment produces a cir- 93. culating system gas which contains more ~ than 5% of carbon dioxide, a loss of gases. will occur.on account of the undesirable reac- tions previously described.

props.statement: If the circulating system gas contains more than 5% of carbon dioxide, a loss of gases occurs through the undesirable reactions: large quantities of methane and carbon monoxide build up and the methanol yield is much lower than theoretically obtainable.

props.name: 3% CO2 with replenishment, or catalyst beds in series

evidence.quote: passing a gas of the pro- _ - portion of 3% carbon dioxide and 97% hy- 105 drogen into the system under pressure,
the circulating system may be dispensed _ with and a gas of the correct proportions ,). may be passed through a number of catalyst beds in series,

props.statement: The small proportion of carbon dioxide may also be used by circulating a 3% carbon dioxide / 97% hydrogen gas and gradually adding carbon dioxide and occasionally hydrogen, or, without a circulating system, by passing a gas of correct proportions through a number of catalyst beds in series under pressure.

props.name: process not dependent on a specific catalyst

evidence.quote: My process is in no way dependent on the use of a specific catalyst.
In general, any catalyst suitable for synthetic methanol pro-- go duction may be employed in the process, these . catalysts ordinarily consisting of mixtures of _ metallic oxides

props.statement: The process is in no way dependent on the use of a specific catalyst; any catalyst suitable for synthetic methanol production may be employed, ordinarily mixtures of metallic oxides.

props.name: economy lies in avoiding side reactions, not in hourly yield

evidence.quote: While Experiment 2, employing 6.5% car- bon dioxide in the circulating system, gave’ 30 the largest yield of condensate per hour,
the same volume of condensate per hour as was obtained in Experiment 2 may ‘be obtained in Experiment 4 by. merely doubling the amount of catalyst employed,

props.statement: Experiment 2 (6.5% CO2) gave the largest yield of condensate per hour, but this is not of prime importance: greatest economy is attained when all gases removed from the process form methanol and water; the hourly volume of Experiment 2 could be obtained under the conditions of Experiment 4 by doubling the catalyst.

props.name: optimum only with CO2 in extremely small proportion

evidence.quote: and pressures to produce methanol, optimum ‘Yesults are obtained only when the carbon dioxide is present in extremely small propor-

props.statement: In the catalytic interaction of carbon dioxide and hydrogen at elevated temperatures and pressures to produce methanol, optimum results are obtained only when the carbon dioxide is present in extremely small proportion to the hydrogen, far less than the theoretical proportion.

props.name: lowered methanol in condensate due to side reactions

evidence.quote: methanol: in the condensate is attributable NS only to the disadvantageous reactions pre- — ‘viously mentioned,

props.statement: The lowered yield of methanol in the condensate (60% instead of 70%) is attributable only to the disadvantageous side reactions, which decompose carbon dioxide and hydrogen without corresponding methanol production.

props.name: pre-catalyst section removes poisons

evidence.quote: is designed te act as a “pre-catalyst” or puri- — fier, to destroy or absorb any catalyst poisons

props.statement: A first catalyst section acts as a pre-catalyst or purifier to destroy or absorb any catalyst poisons in the gas and so preserve the activity of the main section for the methanol reaction.

props.name: fill circulating system with hydrogen, then feed theoretical make-up gas

evidence.quote: the circu- latory system in which the process operate is _ filled with substantially pure hydrogen gas at 40 a pressure somewhat below the pressure de- _ sired for operation.
a mixture of carbon dioxide and hydrogen’ in the proportions theoretically required to make methanol is supplied to the system.
In this manner a most desirable “static condition” is set up

props.note: the patent states this start-up process is the subject of application Serial No. 154,635 and that the invention does not depend on it
props.statement: The circulating system is filled with substantially pure hydrogen (or a gas with some carbon dioxide) and then supplied with make-up gas of theoretical CO2/H2 proportions at a rate keeping the pressure constant, so that the carbon dioxide at the catalyst is very small and a static condition of unvarying circulating-gas composition is set up.

props.name: static condition reached in the circulating gas

evidence.quote: prior gas analyses showed that a practically q10 . static condition had been reached.

props.statement: With a gas mixture of theoretical proportions a practically static condition is reached in the circulating system after a time: the proportions of methane and carbon monoxide are no longer increasing.

props.name: less CO2 in circulating gas, more methanol in condensate

evidence.quote: Table I indicates that as the percentage of carbon dioxide in the circulating gases was 45 reduced from 11% to 2%, the per cent of _°“ ynethanol in the condensate was increased - from 60.5% to 66%.
The_ percentages of methane and carbon monoxide present in the. circulating system are also reduced _as the 15 result of the dimunition in earbon dioxide.

props.statement: As the carbon dioxide in the circulating gases was reduced from 11% to 2%, methanol in the condensate increased from 60.5% to 66%, and methane and carbon monoxide in the circulating system were also reduced.

props.name: methane, CO, carbon and excess water at theoretical proportions

evidence.quote: I have discovered that when methanol is produced from a mixture of theoretical pro- portions of carbon dioxide and hydrogen,
there is a formation of methane and carbon monoxide in the circulating gas. mixture and, further that free carbon is deposited in the appa- ratus.
Also, the proportion of water found with the methanol when the mixture is re- moved, by: condensation, from the apparatus, is much greater than that that should be formed by the methanol reaction,

props.statement: When methanol is produced from theoretical (or somewhat lower) proportions of carbon dioxide and hydrogen, methane and carbon monoxide form in the circulating gas, free carbon is deposited in the apparatus, and the water with the methanol is much greater than the methanol reaction should form.

props.name: several primary reactions at different rates

evidence.quote: From the results thus attained it appears that there are a number of primary reactions occurring at different rates, rather than one or two simple reactions.
The group of reactions which occur 12 varying degrees is believed to be as follows

evidence.second_reading: The group of reactions which occur in varying degrees is believed to be as follows:— (1) 3H2+CO2⇄H2O+CH3OH; (2) CO2+H2⇄CO+H2O; (3) CO2+4H2⇄CH4+H2O; (4) CO+3H2⇄CH4+H2O; (5) CO+2H2⇄CH3OH; (6) CH4+CO2+H2⇄2CH3OH; (7) 2CO→CO2+C.

props.statement: A number of primary reactions occur at different rates, rather than one or two simple reactions; the group is believed to be (1) 3H2+CO2⇄H2O+CH3OH; (2) CO2+H2⇄CO+H2O; (3) CO2+4H2⇄CH4+H2O; (4) CO+3H2⇄CH4+H2O; (5) CO+2H2⇄CH3OH; (6) CH4+CO2+H2⇄2CH3OH; (7) 2CO→CO2+C.
